Its own rule clauses in MN-minnesota.json carry both halves separately — 'Certain nonfelony cannabis records may be automatically expunged under 609A.055. The BCA identifies eligible records and seals them without an application, petition, or motion' and 'For felony and some other cannabis-related cases, Minnesota created the Cannabis Expungement Board. The Board reviews eligible cases ... (609A.06)'. src/lib/rcap/state-packs/minnesota/pathways.ts splits the same two mechanisms at section level: cannabis_automatic -> 'Minn. Stat. section 609A.055', cannabis_board_review -> 'Minn. Stat. section 609A.06'. The registry carries exactly those two and no third: mn_auto_cannabis_nonfelony ('The Bureau of Criminal Apprehension identifies qualifying non-felony cannabis records and expunges them automatically') and mn_ceb_felony_cannabis ('The Cannabis Expungement Board reviews felony cannabis records on its own initiative and orders expungement or resentencing'), both cited to Minn. Stat. ch. 609A and Laws 2023, ch. 63. Re-check rule: when a compiled pathway label joins two section citations with 'or', decompose it into one component per section, bind each component to the registry track whose mechanismExcerpt describes that component's actor and trigger, and record composed_unit_of_registry_track over the resulting set. officialSource.adjudicationBasis: Read directly from the preserved official bytes. S.C. Code § 16-3-2020(F), as rewritten by 2024 Act No. 213 § 2 (eff July 2, 2024), grants a motion-based EXPUNGEMENT remedy: a victim of trafficking in persons convicted or adjudicated delinquent of a trafficking-article violation, prostitution, or any other nonviolent misdemeanor or Class F felony (defined by reference to § 16-1-20(A)(6)-(9)) may motion the court to expunge; the court may grant on a preponderance finding that participation was a direct result of, or interrelated to, being a victim of trafficking; reasonable notice must go to the original prosecuting agency and to victims per the Victim's Bill of Rights; Act 213 § 6 makes the SECTION 2 rights retroactive. The compiled pathway represents the current post-2024 mechanism in near-statutory language — victim status incl. adjudicated delinquent, the exact offense-class formula, the direct-result-or-interrelated nexus, the preponderance standard, the expungement remedy, and the minor-victim protection — and asserts nothing the statute refutes. It omits the two notice requirements and the express retroactivity note; those deltas are carried as a counsel-review requirement on the E4 row, never as a mapping change. The subsection's separate affirmative-defense clause is a prosecution-stage effect, distinct from the expungement remedy adjudicated here.
